accuracy.evidence: Checked against the DfE Year 2 Animals including humans statutory text (animals, including humans, have offspring which grow into adults) and its guidance on human growth stages, NGSS 1-LS3-1, the NHS child development and puberty pages (teenage years 13 to 19, adult height reached by the late teens), the RSPCA and Jackson Laboratory house-mouse notes (weaned at 3 weeks, mature at about 6 to 8 weeks, given as about 2 months), American Kennel Club growth guidance (small dogs adult at about a year, large breeds up to 2 years, given as 1 to 2 years), and Elephant Voices on elephants maturing after 10 or more years (p5). The kitten coats show variation without claiming any colour genetics.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets children's ideas reported in the Nuffield Primary SPACE research on living processes and in Inagaki and Hatano's work on naive biology: young stay young or do not change ('stay', prediction 3 'kittens for ever'), a young animal can become a different kind ('kind', prediction 3 'dogs', p2, m4), growing backwards in old age ('reverse', prediction 1 'being a baby again', m3), skipping straight from child to adult ('skip', prediction 1 'older adult'), all animals growing up as slowly as people ('fast', prediction 4), and offspring being exact copies of a parent ('same', m4).

lab_distinct.evidence: flaglifest is about growth through stages over time: a draggable age dot on a 0-80 line redraws one person at five proportion sets (big head and short body as a baby, a walking stick and grey hair as an older adult) and marks each stage boundary when reached; a five-person jumble can only be lined up youngest first; three kittens tween into cats beside their ginger and black parents, each keeping its own coat; a mouse, a puppy and a child race on one 0-20 year line with green 'grown-up' bands; and cards sort into changes or stays the same. flagbaby matches babies to mothers, flagcycle builds circular cycles, flaghatch sorts eggs from live birth. Gate lab_distinct passes under 30%.

lab_teaches.evidence: Each idea arrives by doing: dragging the dot shows the person change only at stage boundaries and 'Grow older' at the last stage says people do not grow back; a wrong tap in the order step names which stage comes first; every kitten becomes a cat that looks a bit like, not exactly like, its parents; moving time on by one month or one year flips the mouse to grown-up long before the child; wrong card sorts point back to a baby and a grown-up.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions with tempting wrong options the lab disproves: 'being a baby again' or 'being an older adult' after child (the line shows teenager next), 'dogs' or 'kittens for ever' (the kittens grow into cats), and 'the child' or 'they all take the same time' for growing up first (the mouse is grown up within months and the child needs 18 years).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge questions with six distinct feedback messages naming the slip: young grow into the same kind of animal; young do not stay young; life stages only go one way; no stage is skipped; different animals take different times with the mouse and child figures; and young look like their parents but not exactly. Answer order rotates.

readability.evidence: Kid explanation reads at FK grade 2.1 with short sentences using baby, child, teenager, adult, kitten, puppy; adult text averages 8.1, under the 9.5 limit, with one denser paragraph on mistakes. Lab steps are one or two sentences; stage names appear as chips and buttons; times are given in months or years with words, never as decimals.

no_filler.evidence: Gate finds no filler phrases. Each kid paragraph carries one idea (young grow into adults, the five stages in order, like the parents, different growing times). Items vary: p3 counts years until 18, p4 adds kittens and puppies, m5 counts a puppy's months to grown-up, m6 places a 15-year-old in a stage, m8 counts chicks still growing, m9 names a lamb.

mobile.evidence: Checked iPhone 13 screenshots in light and dark for the start state and after Show me on each step: the person and age line fit at 390 px and the stage tick labels now alternate above and below after 0 and 3 collided; jumbled stage chips alternate height after 'older adult' and 'teenager' touched; kittens were enlarged after the first pass made them too small to tap; black cats gained a light outline in dark theme; race lanes and the 0-20 year labels fit the width; buttons wrap to two rows.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button: Grow older and Back to baby, one button per life stage for ordering, Grow a kitten, +1 month, +1 year and +6 years for the race, and Changes or Stays the same. The canvas aria-label is rewritten with each result (stage reached and what it means, which animal has grown up and when, why a card changes or stays). Challenge feedback is a polite live region; walk.cjs axe WCAG 2.1 AA is clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13.
